instruction.text: Most of the sporting events at the ancient Olympics have continued into the modern day. Select the three images of Olympic sports.
This is the discus throw. Select the discus to learn more.

feedback.end: The discus throw first started in the ancient Olympics and continues to be popular today! The discus that the athletes had to throw was very heavy and usually made of bronze.

instruction.text: This is wrestling. Select the athletes’ arms to learn more.

feedback.end: Wrestling was a great way for athletes to practise fighting each other without weapons and to show off their strength. The match would end when one of them fell to the ground three times or surrendered.

instruction.text: This is a running race. Select the athlete in the lead to learn more.

feedback.end: There were three different running events. One of them was just a short sprint along the length of the stadium, while another was running roughly 20 lengths! One length was a little under 200 metres.

instruction.text: This is the race in arms. Select one of the shields to learn more.

feedback.end: In this race, the athletes carried shields and wore helmets — just like when fighting in battle! Warriors were good at this because they were already used to doing it.

instruction.text: Drag the images of sports played at the ancient Olympics to the correct names.

feedback.finish: Other sports included the long jump, javelin throw and chariot racing. Team sports weren’t played at the ancient Olympics.
